## 1. Sri Lanka tabled the 2027 budget projecting a 4.5% deficit and a Rs 2 trillion public‑investment plan.

Total expenditure was set at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 7.93 trillion</span> including a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 260 billion</span> supplementary allocation for Cyclone Ditwah recovery, while revenue and grants were estimated at Rs 6.18 trillion. The Government targeted a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">primary surplus</span> (the Budget balance before interest costs) of 2.3% of GDP and kept the overall gap within the 5% ceiling under the Public Financial Management Act.

Interest payments were put at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 2.64 trillion</span>, roughly 43% of projected receipts, underscoring the weight of debt service on the fiscal accounts. Capital outlays of about 5.1% of GDP focused on grid stability, battery storage, transport links and drinking‑water schemes.

A multi‑year railway electrification got an initial Rs 80 billion, while expressway sections, bridges and urban flood control were funded. The Budget also widened personal income tax bands, cut CESS on 800 tariff lines by 25% and exempted printed books and exercise books from VAT (value‑added tax, a tax on consumption).

## 2. Fitch Ratings said the 2027 budget remained consistent with debt reduction.

The agency noted the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2.3% of GDP</span> primary surplus target could be exceeded if capital spending execution again falls short, as happened in 2026. It assessed the wider <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">4.5% of GDP</span> deficit as compatible with falling debt so long as revenue gains are maintained and expenditure stays within the new fiscal rules.

Its analysis highlighted that interest would absorb about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">41% of Government revenue</span> in 2027, still far above the median for 'B' peers. It also flagged the carry‑forward of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 260 billion</span> in unspent Ditwah funds and said alignment with the IMF programme supported the seventh review.

## 3. The Inland Revenue Department exceeded its 2026 target with Rs 2.44 trillion collected.

Receipts reached <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 2,441.9 billion</span> by November 16 against a full‑year goal of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 2,402 billion</span>. Collections were up by <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 491 billion</span> from the comparable period in 2025, which the department attributed to stronger administration and higher compliance.

The over‑performance provides breathing room ahead of the year‑end and supports the Budget’s consolidation path. Sustaining the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">revenue‑to‑GDP</span> ratio near its 2025 level will be critical to meeting the 2027 primary surplus goal.

## 4. The Cabinet approved a Rs 5.96 billion pumping station at Oliyamulla to cut Kelani River backflow flooding.

Stage I will install <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">15 m3/s</span> (cubic metres per second) of pumping capacity where the Mudun Ela catchment meets the river, with Stage II to add a further 20 m3/s. The project, planned for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2027–2031</span> with <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Japan International Cooperation Agency</span> support, targets reverse flows that inundate low‑lying urban areas when the river runs high.

Officials said Peliyagoda and Pethiyagoda outfalls are part of the same system being upgraded to improve discharge during peak rainfall. The programme complements earlier canal clearance and storage expansion to address urban flash‑flood risk.

## 5. A major LPG supplier reduced cylinder prices after a sharp mid‑month increase.

The 12.5 kg refill was cut to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 5,995</span> and the 5 kg refill to Rs 2,398 after a hike had lifted them to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 6,740</span> and Rs 2,720, respectively. The company cited higher <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Saudi Aramco</span> contract prices, freight and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">financing costs</span>, and said it would absorb losses to prioritise consumer relief.

## 6. The rupee edged weaker against the US dollar on the latest Central Bank reference rates.

The buying rate moved to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 328.37</span> from Rs 328.33 and the selling rate to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 337.27</span> from Rs 337.23. The modest shift keeps the currency broadly stable while external obligations remain front‑loaded into <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">2027–2028</span>.

## 7. The Cabinet approved a National Nuclear Security Coordination Committee under the science ministry.

The body will harmonise policy, threat assessment and operational response across defence, legal and regulatory agencies to meet <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">International Atomic Energy Agency</span> standards (IAEA, the UN’s nuclear watchdog). It will be chaired by the ministry secretary, with the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Atomic Energy Regulatory Council</span>’s Director General as secretary.

## 8. A parliamentary oversight panel backed GPS and satellite collars to track wild elephants.

Members cited obstructed corridors and habitat loss as drivers of rising conflict and called for <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">early‑warning networks</span> and local joint committees. Veterinary support, field anaesthesia risks and mobile equipment needs were also reviewed.

## 9. The Government raised the empowerment grant for low‑income households and expanded coverage.

The maximum capital grant under the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">World Bank‑funded</span> Social Security Project rose to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 200,000</span> from Rs 150,000, with beneficiary families increased to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">11,500</span> from 10,975. The programme targets poor <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Aswesuma</span> recipients to shift towards sustainable livelihoods.

## 10. The stock market snapped a four‑session slide as the ASPI reclaimed the 21,500 mark.

The benchmark gained 0.66% to close at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">21,543.12</span>, while the S&P SL20 rose 0.75% to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">6,142.43</span>. Turnover was <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs 1.73 billion</span> with <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">crossings</span> concentrated in banking shares and foreigners posting a modest net outflow.
